WithinHostExperiment: Within-Host Pathogen Variant QC, Diversity, and Bottleneck

Source: R/WithinHostExperiment-package.R
WithinHostExperiment-package.Rd

Provides a RangedSummarizedExperiment-class-based container and workflow functions for analysing intra-host single nucleotide variants (iSNV) from pathogen deep sequencing data.

Details

The package fills an infrastructure gap between upstream variant callers (iVar, LoFreq, Freebayes) and downstream transmission bottleneck workflows. Its core contribution is replicate-aware, uncertainty-preserving quality control – variants are flagged rather than deleted, preserving full provenance for reproducible analysis. Standardised export functions provide interoperability with tools such as ViralBottleneck.

Key function groups

Import

readWithinHost (from VCF), readWithinHostTable (from TSV/CSV)

Quality control

ISNVFilter (configure thresholds), flagISNV (apply standard QC), flagReplicateDiscordance (replicate-aware QC), flagPrimerSites (amplicon primer masking), qcSummary (QC report), passedISNV (extract clean subset)

Diversity

calcDiversity, shannonISNV, piISNV, wattersonISNV, compareDiversity

Transmission analysis

transmissionPairs, exportPairFrequencies, asViralBottleneckInput, calcSharedVariants, quickBottleneck

Neutrality tests

tajimaD, fusFs, calcNeutralityTests, simpsonISNV, chao1ISNV

Annotation

annotateGenes (labels each site with the genes it overlaps, taking gene ranges as a GRanges or TxDb), annotateCodonChange (the codon and amino acid consequence of each SNV, from VariantAnnotation::predictCoding(), taking CDS records as a GRanges, GRangesList or TxDb and the reference as a DNAStringSet)

Selection analysis

pNpSWithinHost (within-host pN/pS), consensusSequences (per-sample consensus sequences as a DNAStringSet, for dN/dS between hosts with MSA2dist), estimateSelectionCoefficient

Multi-caller consensus

consensusISNV, calcCallerConcordance, benchmarkCallers

Longitudinal analysis

trackFrequency, detectEmergingVariants, plotFrequencyTrajectory

Exact bottleneck estimation

exactBottleneck

Strand bias

sciStrandBias, flagStrandBiasSCI

Temporal QC

flagTemporalInconsistency (longitudinal consistency filtering – flag transient iSNVs that appear at only one timepoint)

Cross-contamination detection

detectCrossContamination (identify index- hopping signatures between co-sequenced samples)

Adaptive filtering

adaptiveFilter

Diversity modelling

fitDiversityModel, checkDiversityPlausibility

Site frequency spectrum

WithinHostSFS-class (S4 class), buildSFS and buildSFSList (construct from WHE), correctSFSBias (ascertainment bias correction), neutralityFromSFS (Tajima's D + Fu's Fs + Fay & Wu's H from a single SFS), compareSFS (chi-squared SFS comparison), plotSFS (publication-quality SFS plot)

Visualisation

plotFrequencySpectrum, plotPairScatter, plotQCDashboard

Scope and limitations

Single-site iSNV resolution

This package operates at the level of individual single nucleotide variants (iSNVs). It does not perform haplotype phasing or quasispecies reconstruction, which require read-level (BAM) analysis that is outside the scope of RangedSummarizedExperiment-based containers. For haplotype-aware within-host analysis, consider CliqueSNV (Knyazev et al. 2021 Nucleic Acids Res 49:e102), ShoRAH (Zagordi et al. 2011 BMC Bioinformatics 12:119), or similar tools. Their output can be imported into WithinHostExperiment for downstream diversity and QC analysis.

Co-infection vs diversity

Distinguishing genuine within-host evolution from co-infection (superinfection) requires phylogenetic analysis of full haplotypes. The multi-caller consensus and replicate-concordance modules reduce artefacts but do not resolve this distinction.

Selection coefficient estimation

estimateSelectionCoefficient assumes a simple deterministic model. For stochastic (drift-aware) estimates, consider dedicated population-genetics frameworks.

Design philosophy

  1. Flag, don't delete. QC functions mark variants in the qcPass assay rather than removing rows, preserving uncertainty and enabling re-analysis with different thresholds.

  2. Replicate-aware. Technical replicate concordance is a first-class QC criterion, not a post-hoc check.

  3. Interoperable, don't reinvent. The package provides standardised export functions compatible with existing downstream tools rather than reimplementing their methods.

  4. Bioconductor-native. Built on RangedSummarizedExperiment, interoperable via VRanges coercion.

References

Roder AE et al. (2023). Optimized quantification of intra-host viral diversity in SARS-CoV-2 and influenza virus sequence data. mBio 14:e01046-23. doi:10.1128/mbio.01046-23

Bendall EE et al. (2023). Rapid transmission and tight bottlenecks constrain the evolution of highly transmissible SARS-CoV-2 variants. Nat. Commun. 14:272. doi:10.1038/s41467-023-36001-5

Sobel Leonard A et al. (2017). Transmission Bottleneck Size Estimation from Pathogen Deep-Sequencing Data, with an Application to Human Influenza A Virus. J Virol 91:e00171-17. doi:10.1128/JVI.00171-17

Mostefai F et al. (2024). Refining SARS-CoV-2 intra-host variation by leveraging large-scale sequencing data. NAR Genomics and Bioinformatics 6:lqae145. doi:10.1093/nargab/lqae145

Zheng B, Johnson PCD, Hughes J (2025). ViralBottleneck: an R package for estimating viral transmission bottlenecks from deep sequencing data using multiple methods. Virus Evolution 11:veaf071. doi:10.1093/ve/veaf071
